GATE_BEFORE_ANY_TRANSFER_ARM_MAY_RUN.rule: MANDATORY_IMPLEMENTATION C: 'Transfer starts only after MCGS_HIDDEN_INFO = PASS or PARTIAL_WITH_MEASURED_IMPROVEMENT, and BYTERL_REFERENCE_FIDELITY = PASS.'
GATE_BEFORE_ANY_TRANSFER_ARM_MAY_RUN.why_it_is_a_gate_and_not_a_preference: a transfer arm measures whether a ByteRL component improves corrected MCGS. If MCGS is not corrected, the arm measures the component against an uncorrected search; if ByteRL is not faithful, it measures a component that is not the published one. Either way the result answers a different question than the one asked, and c021 already produced that result: its transfer arms queried a checkpoint statistically indistinguishable from an untrained floor, so T1/T2 compared MCGS-with-a-near-random-prior against MCGS-with-uniform-random. c021 recorded that as TRANSFER=FAIL; the c022 reconciliation records it as UNTESTED, which is what its own power caveat said.
GATE_BEFORE_ANY_TRANSFER_ARM_MAY_RUN.status_at_time_of_writing: NOT YET MET -- the K sweeps are still running and the ByteRL fidelity probes are complete but the decisive run is not. No transfer arm has been executed.

noise_floor_first.rule: PROBE_MATRIX T05: 'Nominally identical controls estimate run-to-run noise.'
noise_floor_first.why_first: DECISION_RULES §4 defines TRANSFER=PASS as an improvement 'beyond paired run-to-run noise', so the noise floor is the denominator of every subsequent claim. Measuring it AFTER seeing the arms would let the threshold be chosen to fit the answer.
noise_floor_first.design: three nominally identical T0 control arms, differing only in their world-seed base and agent seed, at the same K, protocol, simulation count and game count as the transfer arms. The noise floor is the observed spread of their field scores.
noise_floor_first.c021_value_not_inherited: c021 recorded a 6.4-point run-to-run spread. It is NOT carried forward: c022's arms are simulation-budgeted, use a decision budget, and exclude games differently, so its noise is its own. The c021 figure is recorded alongside for comparison only.
noise_floor_first.additional_evidence_already_in_hand: the contention measurement (results/hardware/contention_tests.json) showed the SAME arm scoring 0.25 and 0.1538 under different machine load, with an identically delivered simulation budget. That is a lower bound on how much a field score can move for reasons that are not the algorithm, and it is why the noise floor is measured rather than assumed.

arms.name: corrected MCGS control
arms.role: the baseline every other arm is compared against; run three times for the noise floor

arms.name: + faithful ByteRL policy prior
arms.hypothesis: a ByteRL prior over which untested action to expand first improves the field score under a finite simulation budget

arms.name: + faithful ByteRL rollout policy
arms.hypothesis: a ByteRL default policy in the rollout improves the field score over uniform random

arms.name: + admitted ByteRL value
arms.hypothesis: a ByteRL value admitted on held-out calibration improves the field score
arms.precondition: PROBE_MATRIX T04 -- runs ONLY after value admission passes. Admission requires the value head to beat a CONSTANT predictor at the observed base rate on held-out games (results/byterl/external_evaluations/*_eval.json, value_calibration.beats_constant_predictor). The measured floor value heads do NOT: skill_vs_constant -0.06 and -0.10.

one_component_at_a_time.rule: MANDATORY_IMPLEMENTATION C and CONTRACT.md §7: 'Do not run a combined hybrid until one isolated component passes.'
one_component_at_a_time.consequence: there is NO T4 combined arm registered. c021 ran a prior+rollout combination arm; it scored below its own control and taught nothing, because with neither component individually established there was no way to attribute the result.
one_component_at_a_time.if_one_component_passes: a combined arm may then be registered as an amendment to this file, with the passing component named.

held_constant_across_every_arm: hidden worlds -- the same world_base_seed per game index, so arm A and arm B search the SAME sampled worlds
agent seed -- derived from the job index alone, never from completion timing (defect D09)
K, budget protocol and simulations per decision
decision budget and the derived per-game wall guard
opponent panel, seat assignment and game count
machine load policy -- every transfer arm runs under the same concurrency, because the contention measurement showed load alone moves a field score by ten points
what_varies: exactly one boolean per arm: expansion_prior, rollout_policy, or value.

verification_that_the_component_is_actua.why: c021 recorded that a transfer arm must 'verify runtime call counts rather than trusting the label'. An arm that names a checkpoint but never calls it is indistinguishable from its own control, and would be reported as 'no effect'.
verification_that_the_component_is_actua.required: every transfer arm must report a nonzero call count for the component it enables, and zero for the components it does not. An arm with a zero call count for its own component is INVALID, not a null result.

decision_rule.PASS: the arm's improvement over the T0 control exceeds the MEASURED noise floor, on paired games with identical worlds and seeds.
decision_rule.INCONCLUSIVE: a positive point estimate smaller than the measured noise floor. DECISION_RULES §4 is explicit that this is neither a pass nor a fail.
decision_rule.FAIL: a regression exceeding the noise floor.
decision_rule.UNTESTED: the arm did not run, or its component was never called, or the checkpoint it queried is statistically indistinguishable from the random floor -- in which case the arm compares MCGS-with-a-random-prior against MCGS-with-uniform-random and answers nothing. This is the status c022 assigns to c021's transfer result.

game_count.basis: TRAINING_AND_EVALUATION §5 requires at least 200 paired games before claiming a six-point effect. At 40 games a Wilson interval spans roughly 15 points, which cannot resolve the effect sizes at issue.
game_count.note: c021's transfer arms ran 34-40 games each. That is the power problem its own caveat identified, and it is not repeated.
